proposals.title: Clocks that stay the same all year
proposals.line: I no longer lose a week of good sleep every spring when the clocks jump forward.

examples.name: American Academy of Sleep Medicine position for permanent standard time
examples.outcome: The academy calls for ending seasonal clock changes and keeping standard time all year

proposals.title: A bedroom that goes properly dark at night
proposals.line: When I switch off the lamp, no streetlight or standby glow gets in, and I wake up less groggy.

examples.name: Northwestern Medicine study of light during sleep
examples.outcome: One night in moderate light (100 lux) rather than dim light (3 lux) raised heart rate during sleep and insulin resistance the next morning

proposals.title: An employer that rewards rest instead of late nights
proposals.line: My workplace treats a full night's sleep as part of doing the job well, and nobody brags about running on five hours.

examples.name: Aetna paying employees for seven hours of sleep
examples.outcome: $25 for every 20 nights of at least 7 hours of sleep, up to $300 a year, logged by a wearable or by hand

examples.name: Crazy Inc. points for a full night's sleep
examples.outcome: Staff who sleep six hours or more on at least five nights a week, tracked by an app, earn points for food in the company cafeteria

overlaps.title: Evenings free from work messages
overlaps.reason: Both describe a workplace that stops eating into the night, one through no messages and one through how rest is valued.

proposals.title: Evenings free from work messages
proposals.line: When I finish work, I'm actually finished, and my phone stays quiet until morning.

examples.name: Portugal Law 83/2021 duty of no contact after hours
examples.outcome: Employers must avoid calling, emailing or messaging workers outside working hours; breaches are a serious administrative offense

overlaps.title: An employer that rewards rest instead of late nights
overlaps.reason: Both describe a workplace that stops eating into the night, one through no messages and one through how rest is valued.

overlaps.title: A full night's sleep between one shift and the next
overlaps.reason: Both protect time off work for sleep; one is about messages, the other about hours between shifts.

proposals.title: Falling asleep without pills or dread
proposals.line: I go to bed expecting to sleep, and most nights I do.

examples.name: HABIT trial of nurse-delivered sleep restriction therapy
examples.outcome: 642 adults; four brief sessions with a practice nurse cut insomnia severity more than a sleep hygiene leaflet, with large effects at 3, 6 and 12 months

examples.name: NICE recommendation of the Sleepio app for insomnia
examples.outcome: A six-week digital CBT-I course at £45 a person, judged more effective than sleep hygiene and sleeping pills; up to 800,000 people in England could benefit

overlaps.title: Insomnia therapy I can follow on my own phone
overlaps.reason: Both end in sleeping well after insomnia therapy; the second differs only in getting it on a phone.

proposals.title: A full night's sleep between one shift and the next
proposals.line: My schedule always leaves me at least 11 hours off between shifts, so I can get home, sleep a full night, and eat before I go back.

examples.name: EU Working Time Directive daily rest and night work rules
examples.outcome: At least 11 consecutive hours of rest every 24 hours; night workers average no more than 8 hours a day, get free health assessments, and can sometimes move to day work

overlaps.title: Evenings free from work messages
overlaps.reason: Both protect time off work for sleep; one is about messages, the other about hours between shifts.

proposals.title: Insomnia therapy I can follow on my own phone
proposals.line: I work through a few weeks of sleep lessons and a sleep diary on my phone, at my own pace, without a waiting list.

examples.name: NICE recommendation of the Sleepio app for insomnia
examples.outcome: A six-week digital CBT-I course at £45 a person, judged more effective than sleep hygiene and sleeping pills; up to 800,000 people in England could benefit

examples.name: Insomnia Coach app from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
examples.outcome: A free five-week CBT-I training plan with a sleep diary, personal feedback, and 17 sleep tools

overlaps.title: Falling asleep without pills or dread
overlaps.reason: Both end in sleeping well after insomnia therapy; the second differs only in getting it on a phone.

proposals.title: No planes over my house at night
proposals.line: Nothing flies overhead between when I go to bed and when I get up.

examples.name: Frankfurt Airport night-flight ban won in court
examples.outcome: No night flights between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m., after two private plaintiffs won urgent applications against the airport's night-flight rules; the City of Offenbach welcomed the ruling

overlaps.title: A street quiet enough to sleep with the window open
overlaps.reason: Both are quieter nights from transport noise near home, from planes and from road traffic.

proposals.title: Small noises no longer jolting me awake
proposals.line: A steady, low sound in my room covers the doors and traffic outside, so I sleep through the little noises.

examples.name: Systematic review of white and pink noise for sleep (Capezuti and colleagues)
examples.outcome: 34 studies of 1,103 adults; 19 reported some improvement, most often for pink noise (9 of 11), but the evidence was weak

overlaps.title: A street quiet enough to sleep with the window open
overlaps.reason: Both end with outside noise no longer waking me, one by covering it in my room and one by removing it from the street.

proposals.title: Napping on a hard day without feeling guilty
proposals.line: When I'm worn out, I lie down for a nap and don't feel I've failed at anything.

examples.name: The Nap Ministry collective napping experiences
examples.outcome: Free group naps of 30 to 40 minutes with mats, pillows and blankets, opening with a meditation and closing with a discussion; founder Tricia Hersey published Rest Is Resistance in 2022

proposals.title: School that starts late enough for my teenager to sleep
proposals.line: My teenager's first class starts at 8:30 or later, so they get up without a fight and sleep about half an hour more.

examples.name: Seattle Public Schools later start time
examples.outcome: High school start moved from 7:50 a.m. to 8:45 a.m.; students slept about 34 minutes more per night, and grades in the studied class rose 4.5%

examples.name: California Senate Bill 328 school start times
examples.outcome: Public high schools can't start before 8:30 a.m. and middle schools before 8 a.m., with compliance due by July 1, 2022

proposals.title: Sleeping in separate rooms so we both rest
proposals.line: My partner and I both sleep through the night, even if that means separate rooms some nights.

examples.name: American Academy of Sleep Medicine survey on couples sleeping apart
examples.outcome: Over a third of U.S. adults sleep in another room from their partner occasionally or consistently; 45% of men and 25% of women

proposals.title: Knowing whether my snoring is sleep apnea
proposals.line: I found out what my snoring means and got it treated, so I wake up clear-headed instead of foggy.

examples.name: American Academy of Sleep Medicine on undiagnosed sleep apnea
examples.outcome: About 30 million U.S. adults have obstructive sleep apnea, and about 23.5 million of them are undiagnosed; CPAP, oral appliances, positional therapy and surgery treat it

examples.name: Apple Watch sleep apnea notification
examples.outcome: FDA-authorized over-the-counter feature on Series 9, Series 10 and Ultra 2 that flags possible sleep apnea after 10 nights of data within 30 days

proposals.title: A street quiet enough to sleep with the window open
proposals.line: Through traffic and loud motorbikes no longer pass under my window at night, so I can leave it open and still sleep.

examples.name: Barcelona superblocks health evaluation
examples.place: Barcelona, Spain (Poblenou, Sant Antoni and Horta)
examples.outcome: Residents and workers in all three of the first superblocks reported less noise and better sleep quality after streets were closed to through traffic

examples.name: Paris noise radar for loud vehicles
examples.outcome: A radar on a lamp post in the 20th district measures each passing vehicle's noise and reads its license plate, with fines planned from 2023
